data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003 redefines reliability as catastrophic-failure reduction and proposes a 'near-miss' (a critical error nearly made but caught by a checklist item) as single-evaluation evidence. But it specifies no causal mechanism for how the near-miss came to be caught: a checklist item can only trigger on a foreseen error pattern. If the near-miss is caught because the checklist happened to list that specific failure, that is exactly compliance tracking the right answer rather than evidence of robustness against the error class. The target never establishes that observing one caught near-miss is evidence of bottom-tail elimination rather than of a checklist that happened to cover that one case, so the proposed evidence does not distinguish genuine reliability gain from lucky checklist compliance.
